problems: Day 31 (tao-dry-d031-p): the key verse includes the line 戰勝，以喪禮處之 (the victor ... according to those rites), and the Heshang Gong commentary's own comment on that line sets the limit rule 6 requires be carried: 明君子貴德而賤兵，不得以而誅不祥，心不樂之 (the gentleman prizes virtue and despises arms, punishes only when he cannot avoid it, and takes no joy in it). The reading gives only the grief of 傷己德薄; revise it within the cap to add that limit, e.g. “... so that the innocent were harmed, and takes the victor’s mourning rites as marking that a ruler who prizes virtue uses arms only when he cannot avoid it”. The SOURCES note calls this ‘the line after the key verse’, but it is inside the key verse.

Day 8 (tao-dry-d008-p): the closing images ‘stopping when dammed and flowing when released’ are left without their point, so a reader cannot see why they matter; the commentary gives them as its gloss on 夫唯不爭 with 聽從人也 (it yields to people). Tie the image to not striving, e.g. “... and its not striving as yielding to people, stopping when dammed and flowing when released”. In the same sentence, drop the doubled ‘takes’ (the plain sense has water ‘takes the low place’, then the commentary ‘takes the highest excellence’) and the repeated phrase ‘the highest excellence’, for example by writing ‘occupies the low place’ in the plain sense.
